cūr

interrogative adverb · Wiktionary

why?

Quō īmus? — Cūr?: the boy’s own travel questions in the libellī.

Other words

  • quārē — why? for what reason?

    adverb (quā rē) · also used · classical · Catull. 85.1: quārē id faciam, fortasse requīris; Mart. 1.32.1: nec possum dīcere quārē; Traupman 407 · Wiktionary

    Also “and so, therefore” (Catull. 1.8).

  • quam ob rem (quamobrem) — why? for what reason?

    phrase: ob with the accusative of the relative · also used · classical · Ter. And. 862: Quamobrem? — Quia libet.; Traupman 138, 407

    Also relative, “which is why” (see “due to”).

  • quid — why? what … for?

    accusative of the interrogative pronoun · also used · classical · Hor. S. 1.1.69: quid rīdēs?; Ter. And. 979: Quid stās? quid cessās? · Wiktionary

    The impatient “why”: “what are you standing there for?”. Quid ita?, why so?

  • quid est quod (+ indicative) — why is it that …? what is the reason that …?

    also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 1.6: etenim quid est, Catilīna, quod jam amplius exspectēs (Lewis & Short s.v. amplus); Traupman 111, 406

    Literally “what is there, that …”. Traupman gives the indicative; Cicero has the subjunctive when the question implies there is no reason.

Examples

  • Quamobrem? — Quia libet.

    Why? — Because I want to.Ter. And. 862

  • cūr ego tēcum nōn sum? cūr ocellōs Ītaliae, vīllulās meās, nōn videō?

    Why am I not with you? Why can’t I see the jewels of Italy, my little country houses?Cic. Att. 16.6.2

  • quid rīdēs? mūtātō nōmine dē tē fābula narrātur

    why are you laughing? Change the name, and the story is about youHor. S. 1.1.69–70

  • clūdere quae cēnās lactūca solēbat avōrum, dīc mihi, cūr nostrās inchoat illa dapēs?

    lettuce used to end our grandfathers’ dinners: tell me, why does it begin ours?Mart. 13.14.1–2

  • ōdī et amō. quārē id faciam, fortasse requīris. nesciō, sed fierī sentiō et excrucior

    I hate and I love. Why do I do it, perhaps you ask. I don’t know, but I feel it happening, and I am in tormentCatull. 85.1–2

  • quā causā

    why, for what reasonTraupman 407

  • cūr, malum, …?

    why the devil …?Traupman 407

See also where are we going?, due to, therefore, what.
